text:
The expected number of non‑zero codewords of weight ≤ \(n-k\) in a random \([n,k]\) code is  
\[
\mathbb{E}[N]=\binom{n}{k}(q-1)^{\,n-k}q^{k-n}\;=\;\binom{n}{k}\Bigl(1-\frac1q\Bigr)^{\,n-k}\;.
\]

Under the assumptions \(k/n\to0\) and \(\frac1q\binom{n}{k}\to\lambda\), the factor \(\bigl(1-\frac1q\bigr)^{n-k}\) tends to 1, and therefore \(\mathbb{E}[N]\to\lambda\).

For large \(n,q\) the numbers of low‑weight codewords become asymptotically independent, so \(N\) converges in distribution to a Poisson random variable with mean \(\lambda\). Hence the probability that no such codeword exists—that is, that the code attains the Singleton bound and is MDS—converges to the Poisson “zero” probability:

\[
\boxed{\displaystyle \lim_{n,q\to\infty}\Pr[C\text{ is MDS}] = e^{-\lambda}}.
\]

ANSWER: \(e^{-\lambda}\)
